one_liner: WooCommerce is a self-hosted WordPress store plugin with a broad REST API (wc/v3) authenticated by merchant-generated consumer key/secret; no central OAuth2, so each store needs its own setup.
auth_notes: Consumer key/secret generated per store in WP admin; over HTTPS sent as Basic Auth (key=username, secret=password) or query params. OAuth 1.0a HMAC-SHA1 signing for non-HTTPS stores. WordPress Application Passwords are used for the MCP route. No OAuth 2.0 in core.
access_notes: WooCommerce is free and open source; no developer programme. Anyone with a store creates keys in WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API. Requires a store with pretty permalinks, and the base URL is per-store.
blocker_notes: Each merchant runs their own store at their own URL, so users must supply the store URL and manually generate consumer key/secret. There is no central OAuth app. The API itself is free and well documented.

evidence.quote: Over HTTPS, send the Consumer Key as the Basic Auth username and the Consumer Secret as the password, or pass consumer_key and consumer_secret as query parameters.
WooCommerce implements OAuth 1.0a signing with HMAC-SHA1 and no token exchange step
Pre-generated keys can be used to authenticate use of the REST API endpoints.
There is no developer programme and nothing to apply for.
Go to **WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API**.
This allows WC data to be created, read, updated, and deleted using requests in JSON format and using WordPress REST API Authentication methods and standard HTTP verbs
With the MCP Adapter plugin, AI clients can discover and run these store operations through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), subject to WordPress and WooCommerce permissions.
Connect an external Model Context Protocol (MCP) client to your store’s WooCommerce AI server.
